title: Text Node
body:
The other [[DOM]] node type: the literal characters between tags. Text nodes have no tag name, no attributes, no classes, and no children. They are leaves. ```html
text

hello

``` That `
` has **three** children, not one: the text node `" text\n\t"`, the `

` [[Element Node]], and another text node holding the whitespace after it. Whitespace and line breaks in the source are real text nodes, which is exactly why [[firstChild]] usually is not the element you were looking for. You almost never create one directly. Setting `element.textContent` makes one for you and throws away whatever children were there before; reading it concatenates the text of every descendant. See [[Modifying Documents]] and [[Node Object]].
